input.question: What kind of cells are generated in scars? Why are some different than its' original cells
input.ground_truth: The cells produced are "backup cells". They are long cells arranged parallel to each other in order to regrow as fast as possible. Unfortunately, these cells are not as strong and may not match the original tissue.

Okay! Let’s imagine your skin is like a big blanket. When you get a cut and it heals, a scar forms. 

When you get hurt, your body sends special workers called cells to fix the blanket (your skin). But these workers don’t always fix it *exactly* the same way as before. 

Instead of making the same kind of blanket squares (which are called "normal skin cells"), the workers make a different kind of blanket square. These new squares are a bit tougher and stickier, like using duct tape instead of soft fabric. That’s why scars feel and look a little different from the rest of your skin—they’re made of different kinds of cells that help the skin stay strong, but they’re not exactly the same as before.
